chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: Consider an ndarray nd1.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: I'm going to show you now how to access cells within that.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: Now the notation at first might seem sort of familiar, but

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: there's some new and different things that you probably haven't seen before.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: So the usual syntax is the name of your ndarray, bracket, the row, and the column.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: So again, these are our rows.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: So row indicates which row we're using, column which column.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: It's important to know that in NumPy, our columns and rows begin at 0.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: So this element is nd1, bracket 0, 0.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: It then continues, of course, 1, 2, 3, 4 in the rows, and

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: in the columns 0, 1, 2, 3.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: Before I tell you, see if you can guess how to address this cell.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: The answer is that this cell is nd1, 3, 2.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: Now this is probably the kind of stuff you've seen before.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: It turns out though that NumPy is much more powerful and

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: can do interesting and different kinds of slicing.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: What if for instance you wanted to address this sub portion of the ndarray?

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: How could you indicate that?

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: NumPy uses a special symbol, the colon, to let you indicate ranges.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: So we can indicate this range in rows with 0, 3, which indicates the 0th to

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: the just before the third row.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: And in the columns, we've got 0, 1, 3.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: So this syntax indicates starting at the 0th row to just before the third.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: And the first column to just before the third.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: And in fact captures this region.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: The key thing to remember here that's a little bit tricky is that this last value is

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: one past the one that you actually want to include.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: So for instance, this is column 3, but it's not included.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: Now if we just use the colon by itself, that indicates, for instance,

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: if we place it in the rows position, that we want all of the rows.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: So you don't have to use the colon just to indicate a range.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: You can use it by itself for all of them.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: Now look at this statement.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: See if you can figure out which part of this indy array it refers to before I show you.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: It is this region right here.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: So it's all the rows and column 3.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: So it's this section right here.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: NumPy includes some special syntax that lets you refer to the last row or column.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: So for instance, the last row here you can indicate with negative 1.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: Second to last row would be negative 2.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: So if we wanted to refer to these two cells here,

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: we would take advantage of this negative 1 syntax.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: So negative 1 indicates that last row.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: And then to get these two columns, we would use 1 colon 3.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: 0, 1, 2, and then we don't include the last one there.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: There is a bunch of new syntax.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: I hope that you find it exciting.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: This is really one of the most powerful aspects of Python and NumPy.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: And it really enables you to do some interesting things.

chunks.title: Notes on Notation
chunks.text: Now we've got a quiz to see if you can figure out how to use this new syntax yourself.
